title: Hearing Teddy Wilson and John Hammond financing the trip to Chicago
summary: Roy Eldridge led him to hear Teddy Wilson with Speed Webb; Hammond paid for Carter to fetch him from Chicago.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yes, that was about 1933, when I had been playing with Fletcher sometime before then, we were playing a date in Providence, Rhode Island, and following that engagement that night, we had a night off. Roy Eldridge suggested we drive up to hear Speed Webb and Speed Webb had a very fine pianist that Roy thought I would like.
So we went up there, and I heard the pianist and I was just oh, tremendously impressed - and it was Teddy Wilson.

And after that time, I went back, you know, after leaving Fletcher while I was in this rehearsal phase of my orchestra, I was being assisted by John Hammond, who was giving me a lot of encouragement, helping me get the guys together, and then he suggested to me, well, if I really liked this pianist this well, whom he hadn't yet heard, he said, 'Why don't you try to get him?'

So I figured how could I get him out of Chicago; he was working in Chicago, and I had no money -- nobody had any money. John said, 'Well, I'll let you have the money to go after him,' you know? So John financed my trip to Chicago and I did go, drove to Chicago with a friend -- a very good friend whose name was George Ritch -- and I'll have more to say about George Ritch later because he figures kind of in my whole career a bit -- what was I talking about?
Teddy Wilson, you went out to Chicago.

Oh yes. So I went out to Chicago, and Teddy Wilson was playing at this place, I think it was called the Golden Lily. Something like that -- it was a Chinese restaurant. And I talked to Teddy, and he finally consented to come to New York -- because I guess I had some recording dates, a few dates that I was looking forward to, but I guess he realized that there might be more opportunity to further his career in New York than in Chicago, as well, you know.
